about: Base components for agent-built UI. Rust validates trees against this file (src-tauri/src/ui_library.rs) and React renders them (src/components/ui-render.tsx). Keep the two in step when adding one. Each primitive lists the libraries it is built on in `uses`; a component's libraries are the union over the primitives it contains.

stack.description: Lays children out in a row or column.

grid.description: Equal-width columns that wrap onto rows.

card.description: A bordered panel with an optional title and description.

text.description: A line or paragraph of plain text.

code.description: A block of code or command output.

badge.description: A short label, e.g. a status.

stat.description: A headline number with a label and optional change.

chart.description: A bar, line or area chart over one x field and up to 5 series on a single y axis (never two y scales; put measures of different scale in separate charts). Always shows a legend for 2+ series and lets the user flip to a table of the data. More than 5 series: keep the biggest and fold the rest into an "Other" series.

x.description: Field of each row used for the x axis.

series.description: [{ key, label }] — fields plotted as series, in a fixed order.

diagram.description: A Mermaid diagram: sequence, flowchart (architecture, network, service maps, data flows), entity-relationship, state, class, gantt. `text` is Mermaid source. Themed with the app (light and dark), sanitised, no click handlers.

map.description: An interactive map (OpenStreetMap tiles) with labelled markers. Fits all markers unless center/zoom are given.

timer.description: A live clock that ticks in the app without you re-rendering: a countdown `until` a time (e.g. a cron's next run) or elapsed time `since` one (e.g. a sub-agent that is running). Times are ISO 8601 or epoch milliseconds.

done.description: Shown when a countdown reaches zero. Without it, the timer shows "overdue 3m 12s" and keeps counting, in a danger colour.

live.description: Keeps its children fed with data the app reads itself (see `sources`), refreshed every `every` ms without you re-rendering. Children bind the latest result as {{data}} (or the name in `as`), and with `history: N` the last N samples as {{history}}: [{ t: "14:03:21", …the numeric fields of each sample }] for charts over time. Shows when it last updated, and errors in place.

source.description: A source, e.g. { kind: "system" } or { kind: "postgres.query", connection: "shop", sql: "select …" }.

every.description: Refresh interval in ms (minimum 1000). Omit to read once (with a refresh button).

as.description: Name to bind the latest result to. Default "data".

form.description: Collects the user's input. Put inputs (textfield, choice, select, slider, rank, toggle) and any layout inside; it adds the submit button. Values stay in the app while the user edits (no message per click). On submit the form locks and shows the answer: with ui_ask the values come straight back to you as JSON; with ui_render they arrive as the user's next message.

textfield.description: A text answer. `multiline` for longer text (e.g. a reply the user edits before it is sent).

name.description: Key of this value in the answer.

choice.description: Pick one option (or several with `multiple`), shown as selectable cards with optional descriptions. Give `correct` (a value or list) for a quiz: once answered, right and wrong picks are marked and `explanation` is shown.

select.description: Pick one from a dropdown, for longer option lists.

slider.description: A number in a range (budget, effort, confidence, priority).

rank.description: Order items by priority (drag or use the arrows). The answer is the list of values, first = most important.

table.description: Rows of data under column headers. Cells are strings or numbers. Columns sort when clicked; tables over 8 rows get a filter box, so pass all the rows rather than a sample.

empty.description: Shown when there are no rows.

find.description: Fill the filter box: shows only rows containing this, so you can point the user at specific rows. Update it in place (same ui_render id) to point elsewhere.

kv.description: Label/value pairs, e.g. details of one item.

list.description: A bulleted or numbered list of strings.

diff.description: A file change shown as removed/added lines.

link.description: Opens a URL in the browser.

button.description: A button. `prompt` sends that text to you (the agent) as the user's next message; `draft` puts text in the user's message box for them to edit and send; `href` opens a URL. Give exactly one.

collapsible.description: A section the user can expand.

tabs.description: Tabbed sections. Children must be `tab` nodes.

image.description: An image, e.g. a screenshot. `src` is an https: or data: URL, or the absolute path of an image file (png, jpg, gif, webp, svg) inside this chat's folders or the system temp folder.

browser.description: A live, interactive preview of a web page in a browser frame. `src` is an http(s) URL (e.g. a dev server on localhost) or the absolute path of a self-contained .html file inside this chat's folders. The page runs sandboxed.

patch.description: A unified diff, e.g. the output of `git diff`, shown per file with hunks and added/removed lines.

tests.description: Test results in green and red: counts, a pass/fail bar, failures first with their messages, passing tests folded away. Give the test command's raw output as `text` (cargo test, pytest -v, go test -v, jest, vitest, node --test, TAP, mix test, rspec); it is parsed here, so pass it as printed. Or give structured `results`.

text.description: Raw output of the test run.

results.description: Instead of text: [{ name, status: "pass"|"fail"|"skip", file?, duration? (ms), message? }].

find.description: Fill the filter (fuzzy on test name and file): shows the matching tests, e.g. the ones you just fixed.

filetree.description: A folder tree you can fold, with file counts per folder. `text` is what `tree` printed (`tree -F` marks folders reliably), or give `paths` (from find, git ls-files, rg --files). Big trees open two levels deep.

paths.description: Instead of text: file paths, one per item.

open.description: Levels open at first. Default: all for small trees, 2 for big ones.

find.description: Fill the search (fuzzy on names; on the path when it has a "/"): opens the folders down to the matches, hides the rest and marks them. Use it to show where something lives, e.g. "refund" or "src/billing/refund.rs".

json.description: JSON with syntax colours, folding and sizes. `text` is JSON as printed by jq, curl or a file (several documents in a row show as a list); or pass `value`. Large values open two levels deep.

value.description: Instead of text: any JSON value.

find.description: Fill the search: a key, a value, or a path like "customer.email" or "items.0.sku"; opens down to each match and marks it.

textfile.description: A file or long text for reading: what `cat`, `head` or `sed -n` printed. Fits the size: short text sits inline; longer text gets line numbers, a scroll box and search. `highlight` lines or a `find` scroll the view to them. With a `path`, Markdown renders (raw toggle), CSV/TSV shows as a table and JSON as `json`.

path.description: File path or name; picks the view and is shown as the title.

start.description: Number of the first line, e.g. 40 for `sed -n 40,80p`. Default 1.

follow.description: Keep the view scrolled to the last line as the text grows (logs).

find.description: Fill Find: marks every line containing it and scrolls to the first; the user steps through with Enter. Use with `highlight` to point at code.

wordcount.description: What `wc` printed, as a breakdown: totals, and a bar per file for the main count. Pass `columns` when not the default lines/words/bytes, e.g. ["lines"] for `wc -l`.

columns.description: Which counts each row holds, in order: "lines", "words", "bytes", "chars". Default ["lines","words","bytes"]; a single number per row means lines.

gitgraph.description: Git history as a graph: a colour per lane, refs (HEAD, branches, remotes, tags) as badges, then hash, subject, and author and date when present. `text` is what `git log --graph --oneline --decorate` printed (add --all for every branch; add --format="%h%d %s (%an, %ar)" for author and date).

gitstatus.description: `git status` grouped: branch with ahead/behind, then conflicts, staged, unstaged and untracked files with a badge per change. `text` is what `git status --porcelain=v1 -b` printed (best), or plain `git status`.

diffstat.description: `git diff --stat` (or `git show --stat`, `git log --stat` for one commit) as a bar of additions and deletions per file, largest first.

sql.description: A SQL editor the user runs: syntax highlighting, completion of the connection's table and column names, ⌘↵ to run, results as a sortable table, a history of runs, and "Send to chat" to bring a query and its result back to you. Runs read-only (READ ONLY transaction, 15s timeout, row limit) on a saved connection. Give `sql` to start from; render again with the same id and new `sql` to rewrite it.

connection.description: A connection name from ui_catalog `connections`; the user can switch.

syntax.node: A node is a string (text), or { type, props?, children? } where type is a primitive or a library component name, or a control node.
syntax.bindings: Any string inside props or text can contain {{path}} to insert a value from the component's props (e.g. {{user.name}}, {{items.0}}). A string that is exactly "{{path}}" passes the value through unchanged, so arrays and numbers keep their type.
syntax.each: { each: "path.to.array", as: "item", index?: "i", key?: "id", children: [nodes] } repeats children once per element, with {{item}} and {{i}} bound. Give `key` (a field of each item) whenever the list can change or reorder between renders, so open sections and other UI state stay with their item.
syntax.if: { if: "path", children: [nodes], else?: [nodes] } renders children when the value is truthy (non-empty string/array, true, non-zero).
syntax.components: Using a library component as a node passes its props: { type: "deploy-status", props: { env: "{{env}}" } }.

sources.about: Data the app reads itself. Use with a `live` node (and source_read to look first). GitHub and Linear sources use the connections the user made in Settings → Integrations (read-only; you never see a token). Database sources take a `connection` name from ui_catalog `connections`; credentials never reach you.

system.returns: { host, uptimeSecs, cpu (%), cores: [%], memUsedGb, memTotalGb, memPct, swapUsedGb, load1, load5, load15, disks: [{ mount, totalGb, usedGb, pct }], processes: [{ pid, name, cpu, memGb }] (top 8 by CPU) }

docker.containers.returns: [{ id, name, image, state (running|exited|…), status, ports, created }]

docker.stats.returns: [{ name, cpu (%), memPct, memUsage, netIO, blockIO, pids }] (running containers)

postgres.schema.returns: { connection, tables: [{ schema, table, columns: [{ name, type, nullable }] }] }

postgres.query.returns: { connection, columns: [names in order], rows: [{ column: value }], truncated } — runs in a READ ONLY transaction with a 15s timeout

github.pr.returns: { number, title, url, body, state, stateLabel, draft, author, head, base, additions, deletions, changedFiles, review, reviewLabel, labels: [names], checks: [{ name, state: pass|fail|pending|skipped, tone, mark, url }] (failures first), checksSummary: { pass, fail, pending, skipped, text, tone }, reviews: [{ author, state, body, at }], comments: [{ author, body, at }], files: [{ path, additions, deletions }] }

github.pr.diff.returns: { repo, number, text (unified diff, for `patch`), bytes, truncated }

github.prs.returns: [{ number, title, url, author, branch, draft, review, checks (summary text), checksTone, updatedAt }]

linear.issue.returns: { id, title, url, description, state, stateType, priority, priorityVariant (for badge), estimate, due, assignee, creator, team, teamKey, cycle, project, labels: [names], subIssues: [{ id, title, state, done }], subDone, subTotal, links: [{ title, url }], comments: [{ author, body, at }] }

linear.issues.returns: [{ id, title, url, state, stateType, priority, priorityVariant, estimate, assignee, updatedAt }]

linear.board.returns: { team, teamKey, cycle, columnCount, columns: [{ state, type, count, issues: [rows as linear.issues] }] } — the active cycle's issues by workflow state (open issues when there is no cycle)

linear.cycle.returns: { team, number, name, starts, ends, daysLeft, progressPct, scope, completed, scopeAdded, issues, issuesDone, history: [{ day, scope, completed }] } — the active cycle
